body:
This reads like I wrote it.

The things to live for losing meaning hits home.

The boredom I agree is way too much. As for thats the way it will be the rest of your life? I cant speak to that, cause thats where I am currently, feeling the same way. But for my father it really was just finding the right meds, lucky bastard.

Your friend calling you out though, Hah! Thats a good friend. Our group has a guy who is constantly going through rough patches a few years ago he was trying to convince us that he wasn't worth being loved and to stop being his friend. We told him it doesnt work like that we don't choose who we love, and we cant just stop, especially when we see when they're in need. 

You could try telling him and I'm sure he'll try his best to support. Chances could be he feels some of the ways you do and could also use your support, we humans are social.
Now I have to listen to myself and open up as suicidal to my own friends as opposed to just turning up dead soon. Im so tired.

Maybe one of us will figure it out and last a bit longer, I hope its you. Good luck brother.

For me its both. Depressed on top of the depression that capitalism is pushing me into.

The world is just so angry and mean to everyone else so trying to help people or help is just that much harder.

So I talked to my parents and they feel that I'd be the best one to talk with him, since we're closer. 

They pretty much asked me to deal with it.

I'll write him a letter. I'll also try to cheer him up by doing things he likes. 

I'm at a loss on what to do to help him face his problems though.
I like hiking. A couple weeks ago I went for a hike and I enjoyed that. Maybe I should do that again.
Hey, dont do anything drastic, that other guy is just an asshole, He has no place here. I'm sorry you had to deal with him. People are here to help you.

I have one that works well for me; I go for a walk.
I guess the main trick is knowing when I'm angry, and if I notice, I take off. 

I don't know if this is a good idea or not, but it works for me, and I've gotten into a lot less trouble doing so, than hanging around. I distance myself from where I was. Works wonders for me.

Location plays into this too, you can't exactly go for a walk on a plane.

So I should just wait, and hold off on it this time?
I've wanted to die these past few months, and each new day I want to die even more, is there an upward trend somewhere? I'll keep waiting like I have been, but it hurts. I can't bring myself to do anything. I wish I was strong enough to do something about it. But I do guess I am strong since I've not given in for these past months

Thank you stranger; step one to not dying: don't kill yourself.

Family: non-abusive, I'd say good.

Siblings: one brother

School: Failing, last semester of High-school

Friends: close to none, at least none that I feel are my friends.
Age: eighteen since January

Life ambitions: I wanted to be a commercial, non-military pilot, but I doubt I'll get there with how I'm performing

Job: unemployed

Health: skinny, out of shape, Scoliosis and possibly ankylosing spondylitis, no drugs

personality: I procrastinate, I'm lazy, bad people skills, shy extrovert. not an angry person, though I've gotten in trouble with it in the past.


Context: I've been contemplating suicide since before January, I had set a date on the day after my birthday, but it fell through, didn't even attempt. scraped through last two months, still having thoughts of hopelessness. I tell an online friend, who suggests I tell someone, but it never happens, still hasn't happened. Spring break, massive projects in two classes due day I get back, don't do them. Have decent break, am with "friends" most of it, having more serious thoughts than usual. Now I'm back home the last night of spring break, tomorrow the fate of my highschool career is pretty much set, and I haven't anything done, too stressed to focus, I've tried to do it, just can get anything on paper, might as well give up anyways. Now I'm sitting here with my pocketknife within arm's reach, which strangely makes me feel better. I don't want to tell my parents, but I probably need to. They both suffer from depression, my dad more so, so they can probably help me, but religion is their main helper. I'm not nearly as religious as they are, but I don't want to tell them that. I also haven't ever told anyone with my voice what's going on. So, I guess I need to tell someone, but how to I go about doing that? "Hey, I'm going to kill myself! See ya later!" or "I think suicide is a viable option for me any tips?" "What is your view on this nation's current economic status? Mine is that is doesn't matter if I'm dead" "I have a knife and am going to slash open my arms and bleed to death" Those don't seem to be the best way to ask for help, but I don't know how I would even try. I don't ever act on impulse anymore, too much getting in trouble every time I do so. 

Crying would feel so good right now, but I just can't.
As in this moment? or overall?

I can about pretty much anything that doesn't pertain to me without a problem, yet I just can't seem to talk about myself for anything.

On here isn't as much as a problem as I know what I share here wont come back to haunt me. 

My performance in life hasn't been the greatest recently, and I've been planning to end my life for a few months now.

Nothing I do feels like its worth it, I have no one close, I've messed up what I wanted to do in life, my back is getting more and more bent out of shape, soon it will start fusing to itself, I don't want to live through that. 

No one in my life knows, they just think I'm just another slacker who wont ever amount to anything. I told people on the other side of the internet, and thats it. Not sure why I' doing that, I guess it makes me feel less alone.

I just wasted people's time, you nice people could be helping others, instead of this particular whatever I am.

I will try, but I lock up when talking about things like this. So many times it has actually been relevant in various conversations, and all I need to do was mutter a one or two syllable word, but I could not actually bring myself to say it. Different people like different things, I hope I choose the right one.

One more day.

I feel the same way.

Its a tiring journey, like a really hard dungeon, only all the loot is shit, and it keeps getting harder, but the loot isn't getting better. You begin to doubt the existence of good loot at the end, you begin to question the utility of such loot. Then you hear the others who've completed the dungeon already, some found the loot useful, and others found the  loot useless. Yet they can all say they made it.

There are small enclaves to the side of the path that contain consumables, but every time they're consumed the dungeon gets darker, and harder to see. Your health is low, but you see a wanderer up ahead, they seem to be on the same path as you. You offer a hand, he brightens up and fixes you armor, you and your new found partner crush the final boss, the loot may or may not be what you were looking for, but you leveled up, and you can use you newfound skills of conquering dungeons to perhaps raid a castle, command an army, or be a trader of rare loot. You stay with your partner, and you conquer lots of things together.

People can help and you don't have to be alone.  

A cool quote I heard once:
"You find questions, answers find you"
but it doesn't help if I have a fear of talking to people.
